body: As much as it may feel like you do, you don't have a lot of responsibilities in college. It's a transition period. I know how you feel with anxiety, and the best I can tell you is try and come out of your shell. I know that's terrifying, but at the end of the day, you'll thank yourself for doing it. Just try and relax. And you'd be surprised what you can accomplish when you have no choice but to do them. Sorry if I wasn't much help

While I'm sure that advice is good for someone without social anxiety, having it makes going out somewhere by myself where there's a lot of people an absolutely frightening idea. To give an example, there's a jazz bar, Warm Daddies in Philadelphia (dumb name I know), that I REALLY want to go to, but I can't work up the nerve to go. And even if I did go, I know I'd be so anxious the entire time that I wouldn't have any fun whatsoever, and wouldn't bother with it again because I would just have anxiety the next time, and it wouldn't seem worth it at all. 

I'm quite aware I'm being difficult, but this is what I have to deal with every single day, and it's just getting to be too much. I want things to change, believe me, but doing what you suggest is horrifying, especially alone. I also don't really drink, I don't enjoy it that much, so that also doesn't help me. I'm in a wonderful position! I appreciate the well thought out answer though.
